rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when holding, pulling, or fastening something tight.

example.english: Hold the rope tight, and don't let go.
example.traditional: 你揸緊條繩，唔好放手呀。
example.jyutping: nei5 zaa1 gan2 tiu4 sing4 m4 hou2 fong3 sau2 aa3

rows.note: Use this verb-plus-complement pattern when emphasizing that an action is done firmly or securely, as in gripping something so it will not come loose.

example.english: Hold the bag tight so nobody snatches it.
example.traditional: 揸實個袋，唔好畀人搶走。
example.jyutping: zaa1 sat6 go3 doi2 m4 hou2 bei2 jan4 coeng2 zau2

rows.note: Use 緊 as the all-purpose choice for something physically tight, tightly controlled, close-fitting, or leaving little time or room.

example.jyutping: tiu4 sing2 bong2 dak1 hou2 gan2

rows.note: Use 窄 specifically for a passage or space that is narrow and difficult to pass through.

example.english: This alley is too tight for the car to get through.
example.traditional: 呢條小巷太窄，架車過唔到。
example.jyutping: ni1 tiu4 siu2 hong6 taai3 zaak3 gaa3 ce1 gwo3 m4 dou2

rows.note: Use 手頭緊 when someone has little money available, not when they are stingy.

example.english: I'm tight on cash lately, so I'll pay you back later.
example.traditional: 我最近手頭緊，遲啲先還錢。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zeoi3 gan6 sau2 tau4 gan2 ci4 di1 sin1 waan4 cin2

rows.note: Use 親密 for people or relationships that are emotionally close and intimate.

example.english: We have always been tight with them.
example.traditional: 我同佢哋一向都好親密。
example.jyutping: ngo5 tung4 keoi5 dei6 jat1 hoeng3 dou1 hou2 can1 mat6
